bell-poking (lit.), name of an annual ritual performed at the Banagudi in Ta:ndana:du. Prior to the main ceremony of devva habba/de:va habba (q-v.), Badaga men from Ta:ndana:du go to the Toda hamlets in Ko:dana:du and offer the salt ritual, uppu sa:stara, for Toda buffaloes. The next day a Toda elder from there visits the Banagudi temple at Ta:ndana:du and, in the presence of the Badaga priest, cleans up the premises and burns the debris in a fire made by the priest with fire-sticks . Then a sacred bell kept in that temple is picked up with a stick by the Toda man and deposited in the corner pocket of an embroidered shawl (bugu si:le/buguru si:le) especially worm by the Badaga priest on that day. After a blessing the bell is replaced inside the temple. Only these two men should be present
